research_mode: official ONS and Office for Statistics Regulation sources only; recording-quality governance, inspection, rule-change, survey-design and uncertainty gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Crime data integrity inspection interval
verified_claims: HMICFRS inspects each police force's crime data integrity roughly every three to five years
limitations: the interval means inspection findings are not continuous monitoring

sources.name: Crime-recording sample construction
verified_claims: HMICFRS samples incidents using opening codes where a crime would be expected
limitations: the audit tests a sample rather than every incident

sources.name: Crime-recording offence groups
verified_claims: crime-recording accuracy is checked for violence against the person, sexual offences and all other offences
fraud is excluded because it is recorded only by the City of London Police
limitations: the three-group framework is not an offence-level parcel measure

sources.name: Weighted crime-recording accuracy
verified_claims: HMICFRS weights inspection results to calculate accuracy for each offence group and all crime excluding fraud
limitations: weighted inspection accuracy is not the same as a crime rate

sources.name: Crime-data-integrity grading components
verified_claims: the graded judgement uses recording accuracy plus dip samples, recording timeliness and force management and oversight
limitations: the grade must not be interpreted from accuracy percentage alone

sources.name: 2014 national recording accuracy
verified_claims: HMICFRS estimated 80.5% accuracy with a plus-or-minus 2.0 percentage-point interval in 2014 for all crime excluding fraud
limitations: the estimate belongs to the 2014 inspection design

sources.name: 2021 to 2022 national recording accuracy
verified_claims: HMICFRS estimated 92.4% accuracy with a plus-or-minus 0.3 percentage-point interval by the end of the 2021 to 2022 programme
limitations: later inspections are affected by 2023 counting-rule changes

sources.name: Forces exceeding 90 percent accuracy
verified_claims: 17 of 23 inspected forces recorded more than 90% of reported crime in the 2021 to 2022 programme
limitations: not all forces were inspected in that programme

sources.name: Forces exceeding 95 percent accuracy
verified_claims: 6 of 23 inspected forces recorded more than 95% of reported crime in the 2021 to 2022 programme
limitations: the count is programme-specific and not a current league table

sources.name: Inspection snapshot limitation
verified_claims: HMICFRS inspections use a subset of crimes from the most recent three months
limitations: the findings are a single-point snapshot and cannot provide continuous accuracy

sources.name: Post-2023 inspection comparability
verified_claims: changes to Home Office Counting Rules mean 2023 to 2025 and later inspection findings are not directly comparable with earlier findings
limitations: cross-cycle performance comparisons must remain fail-closed

sources.name: External audit improvement driver
verified_claims: regular external auditing reintroduced in 2014 was a key driver of crime-data-integrity improvements
limitations: association with improvement does not isolate a single causal effect

sources.name: Strong data leadership
verified_claims: senior leadership and chief constables play a critical role in setting data culture and driving recording improvements
limitations: governance evidence is qualitative and force-specific

sources.name: Crime-data governance boards
verified_claims: well-recording forces commonly use crime-data standards or integrity boards with senior officer representation
limitations: board presence alone does not prove accurate recording

sources.name: Recording-performance separation
verified_claims: clear separation between crime-recording teams and performance teams reduces manipulation or gaming risk
an independent force crime registrar increases data integrity
limitations: organisational separation is a control, not a measured crime outcome
